newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains vs forward dollar, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains vs forward dollar, seen rising.

text.p: The Indian rupee opened up against the forward dollar on Friday, dealers said.
January dollars fell to 78/81 paise from the opening level of 80/82 paise on Friday. January dollars closed at 79/82 paise on Thursday.
The premiums are bound to fall further, dealers said.
Dealers attributed the rise to central bank's signals for cutting interest rates and talk of additional measures to achieve this.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday cut the bank rate and the interest on one-year deposit to trigger an interest cut by banks.
Dealers said the RBI governor's statement some newspapers saying the central bank may resort to open market operations to achieve its goals in addition to change of bank rate deepened the sentiment.
Spot rupee was steady at 35.81/82, down from 35.82/83 opening as expected demand from State Bank of India was missing, dealers said.
"The market is full of (dollar) sellers now," said a dealer.
